{{recipe}}

'''Corn pone''' is a small simple corn [[Cookbook:Cake|cake]], similar to a johnnycake. It was originally cooked in ashes, and introduced to early European settlers by indigenous Americans.

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Quart|qt]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* [[Cookbook:Cornmeal|Cornmeal]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] [[Cookbook:butter|butter]]
* [[Cookbook:salt|Salt]] (optional)

==Procedure==
# Put on the water in a pot, and as soon as it [[Cookbook:Boiling|boils]] stir in enough cornmeal to make a very thin [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]].
# Beat it frequently while it is boiling for 10 minutes; remove from the heat, pour it in a pan, and add the butter and salt to taste.
# When the batter is lukewarm, stir in enough corn meal to make it quite thick.
# Let rise overnight.
# Pat the [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] out into small cakes.
# Butter a baking tin and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] in a moderate oven '''or''' butter a [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|cake pan]], fill it ¾ full, and bake. 

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* This recipe did not originally have an oven temperature; 350°F is probably safe.  
* To prevent lumping, mix some cool water into corn meal first, before adding boiling water. See details at [[Cookbook:Mixing#Mixing flours or dry meal with hot liquids|Mixing flours or dry meal with hot liquids]].
